finalRewrite.answer: Each transaction consumes its source account's sequence, so workers sharing one source collide with `tx_bad_seq`. Use funded channel accounts, one lane per worker, as transaction sources; keep the real account as operation source and signer where the operation needs it. After `tx_bad_seq` do not blindly rebuild a payment with a new sequence, which can duplicate it; check the original hash first. `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` is temporary: wait and resubmit the same envelope. An identical signed envelope can be submitted to more than one provider; expect duplicate, pending or not-found responses during lag. An `invalid u32` error usually means a client typing bug, because sequences are 64-bit.
keyFacts: Funded channel accounts as transaction sources give parallel sequence lanes.
After tx_bad_seq, a rebuilt payment with a new sequence can duplicate; check the hash.
TRY_AGAIN_LATER is temporary: wait, resubmit the same envelope; terminal codes need a fix.
An identical signed envelope is hash-idempotent; expect duplicate or pending replies.
avoid: Do NOT submit uncoordinated transactions from one source-account sequence lane.
Do NOT retry terminal result codes without fixing or rebuilding the transaction.
Do NOT promise fixed throughput or treat invalid u32 as a protocol sequence limit.
finalRewrite.notes: Fee-bump replacement for 'same sequence, higher fee' is correct to mention. Multi-provider resubmission rests on hash idempotence plus documented duplicate and pending behavior; no live two-provider run backs it.

finalRewrite.question: What is the OpenZeppelin Relayer on Stellar, how is the relayer account funded, and how do I integrate it with my backend to pay fees?
finalRewrite.answer: OpenZeppelin Relayer is a self-hostable AGPL relaying service. Its Stellar support covers prepared-XDR submission, classic payments, Soroban invocation, fee-bump or sponsorship flows, policies and several signer backends. When self-hosted you configure and fund the relayer account yourself. OpenZeppelin Channels is the separate managed offering with hosted authentication, parallel accounts and fee handling; its hosted service publishes no generic top-up address. Keep credentials and signing server-side, validate transaction intent, and date any release, network-support or service-health claim.
keyFacts: Self-hosted OpenZeppelin Relayer and managed Channels are different products.
Relayer on Stellar supports XDR, payment and Soroban submission, fee-bump and sponsorship.
Self-hosting means funding your own relayer account; Channels has no top-up address.
Release and health claims carry an as-of date; a 401 is not proof of downtime.
avoid: Do NOT conflate self-hosted Relayer with managed Channels.
Do NOT publish a generic hosted top-up address.
Do NOT pin a release, network support or provider health without an as-of date.

finalRewrite.answer: Scaffold Stellar is a separate plugin: `cargo install --locked stellar-scaffold-cli`, then `stellar scaffold init <project>`. It coordinates Rust contracts, TypeScript clients and bindings, a frontend template and environment configuration. It is not part of the core CLI, and it differs from `stellar contract init`, which creates only a contract workspace. As of 2026-11-14 the crate is 0.0.34. Current projects keep networks, accounts and contracts in a version 2 `scaffold.yml`; `environments.toml` is the legacy format, and the Stellar Docs Scaffold page still describes it. Review generated scripts and community templates before running them; local networks need Docker.
